A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Latent Wavelet Diffusion work. All 26 pages of v3 and 30 pages of v4, including appendices, support comparison. Text extraction and visual inspection resolve the relocated tables, figures, and equations.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices C–E report original image-generation comparisons, frequency-sensitive measurements, and VAE reconstruction results.

after.justification: The original empirical results are retained, supplemented by component, transform-choice, masking-bound, and computational-overhead results.

M1.justification: The proposed two-stage procedure retains scale-consistent VAE fine-tuning, Haar-derived saliency, and time-dependent masking of the diffusion loss. The loss equations and default masking bound of 0.3 remain unchanged. Newly tested alternatives are ablation configurations, not replacements for the proposed method.

E1.justification: Aesthetic-4K/Aesthetic-Eval, LAION-High-Res, and HPD prompt coverage remain unchanged, including 2K/4K generation and VAE reconstruction. The added ablations vary components and settings within existing coverage rather than introducing new datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: v4 Table 5 newly evaluates Daubechies db2 and FFT high-pass alternatives against Haar masking. Table 4 also adds VAE-only and masking-only component controls. Comparator membership in the retained generation, reconstruction, and frequency-quality tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: v4 adds component and transform comparisons on the Diffusion4K backbone at 2048×2048 on Aesthetic, a five-value masking-bound sweep, and a single-A100 memory/timing benchmark measured over 20 training steps. Existing benchmark protocols are not substantively revised; the newly explicit baseline-VAE policy documents an existing comparison rather than establishing a rerun.

E4.justification: v4 newly reports component attribution in Table 4, transform selection in Table 5, masking-bound sensitivity in Table 6, and training overhead in Table 10. These substantially expand evidence about component contributions, design choices, and costs. The reconstruction analysis in v4 Section 4.4.1/Table 3 already appeared in v3 Appendix E/Table 5.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same fixed-seed, first-output selection protocol for qualitative examples. v4 introduces no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-estimation procedures; its added quantitative tables report point estimates.

E6.justification: All five original numerical result tables are unchanged after matching their locations. Substantial new diagnostic results include FIDs of 39.50 and 39.20 for the separate VAE and masking controls, and 38.92 and 39.45 for db2 and FFT alternatives. The masking-bound sweep adds a sensitivity trend, while Table 10 reports Sana memory usage of 57.9 versus 60.1 GB with approximately 47 seconds per 20 steps for both configurations.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 changes the definition of T in the masking rule from the total number of training steps to the total number of diffusion timesteps. The mathematical formulas otherwise remain unchanged, including the appendix wavelet and frequency-metric definitions. The expanded transform discussion supplies conceptual reasoning rather than new proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: frequency-guided training improves ultra-high-resolution synthesis without architectural changes or additional inference cost. v4 clarifies that high-resolution generation remains computationally demanding, consistent with the earlier claim about additional inference cost.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations of reduced GLCM scores as a perceptual tradeoff, comparable alignment as a design choice, and Haar's performance through spatial localization and compact support. Appendix A discusses masking-bound tradeoffs and reports no observed benchmark failure cases. The existing VAE-compression limitations and suppression-versus-detail rationale are retained.

D1.justification: v4 reports a released repository containing implementation, training/evaluation code, and checkpoints instead of promising a future release. It newly specifies loss weights α=0.25, β=0.001, λ=0.05, four-A100 hardware, and the tuned-versus-original VAE comparison policy. Most training budgets move unchanged to Appendix D, but v3's explicit 4K Diffusion4K training configuration is omitted. Repository contents were not independently checked.

R1.justification: v4 adds Tragakis et al. (2024), 'Is One GPU Enough?', to the high-resolution generation motivation. Most other reference changes update publication metadata for existing works, including Spectral Image Tokenizer and the wavelet diffusion GAN paper. Positioning relative to Diffusion-4K and attention-guided supervision remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: the existing reconstruction study moves from Appendix E into Section 4.4.1, training recipes move from Section 4.1 into Appendix D, and the previous wavelet and frequency-suppression appendices are consolidated into an expanded Appendix A. Selected explanations are rewritten, administrative statements are added, and author order and affiliations are updated.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 4–6 and 9–10, moves the reconstruction table into the main text, redraws Figure 2, and relocates Figure 3 beside the VAE discussion with an expanded caption. Table and figure placement is substantially reorganized. The generated-image galleries and existing numerical tables are retained; Table 9 largely redisplays previously documented training settings.

improvement.justification: Compared with v3, the new component controls, design-choice ablations, and overhead measurements make the existing method better supported, while explicit loss weights and VAE policies improve reproducibility. These are useful but bounded gains: the new ablations lack uncertainty estimates, Table 6 leaves its dataset/backbone unspecified, and the explicit 4K Diffusion4K training recipe is lost. The revision improves assessability without establishing substantially stronger overall empirical conclusions.
